answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region during peak settlement writes, so the lever that historically restored regional latency without dropping writes is a failover, not more of the same region. Rollback is unavailable because the in-flight build is a non-revertible security patch. Circuit breaking would fail writes and violate the objective. Read-replica routing addresses reporting load, not the write path. Pre-peak headroom is a different play and does not establish that adding boxes now fixes a region-scoped regression. Unverified: whether March failover conditions match today’s settlement peak, whether secondary already carries the patch, and whether cutover could disorder downstream settlement—hence a standard (not blanket) shift and a downstream-value flag. Cause is still inferred from timing and region scope, not proven.
